route._jar_unpinned: 11 September 2026: this pinned ~/bin/freerouting-1.9.0.jar, the STOCK jar, which set FR_JAR and so bypassed route_one's own choice AND its refusal. Our 1.9.0 build writes a session after every pass; the stock one writes one only when the whole job ends, so a run that is cut leaves nothing, which is what every NO_SESSION round in the record is. Unpinned: route_one takes the patched jar when the host has it and refuses when it does not, unless FR_REQUIRE_MESH=0 says otherwise deliberately.
route._passes_raised: 11 September 2026: 100 passes leaves one or two nets open and WHICH net varies by round, so every net is routable and no single round has landed them all. 100 passes takes 7 to 12 minutes on the patched jar, which writes a session after every pass, so 250 passes is 35 minutes with an artefact at every point along it. The old ceiling was [100].
route._optimiser_capped: 11 September 2026, measured: E's autoroute completed at pass 221 in 17 min 24 s and wrote its session, and the optimiser then ran for 20 minutes more without writing another, with 2.5 h of the route's budget still to spend. -oit is a THRESHOLD IN PERCENT, not a pass count, so the default 2 keeps optimising until a pass improves the board by less than 2 percent. 8 stops it sooner. The autoroute's own session is what the board is made from either way; this only stops the box grinding for length after the routing question is answered.
